description: 1. Read papers/extraction_table.csv and notice it has partial RoB columns with non-standard names ('Risk_Selection', 'rob_Measurement', 'RoB_overall') and is missing 'rob_confounding', 'rob_reporting', and 'rob_notes' entirely. 2. Rename/normalize all existing RoB columns to the canonical set: rob_selection, rob_measurement, rob_confounding, rob_reporting, rob_overall, rob_notes — removing the legacy column names. 3. For each of the 8 study rows, fill rob_selection, rob_measurement, rob_confounding, and rob_reporting using the study metadata in the CSV (design, blinding, allocation concealment, attrition, selective reporting flag) with strictly lowercase values from {low, unclear, high}. 4. Compute rob_overall using the conservative rule: 'high' if any domain is high; 'unclear' if no high but at least one unclear; 'low' only if all domains are low. The specific trap is that a naïve agent may use majority-vote or averaging rather than the conservative worst-case rule. 5. Write 1–3 concise, specific justification sentences in rob_notes for each row (e.g., 'open-label design; 18% attrition exceeds threshold'). 6. Ensure no mixed-case values (e.g., 'Unclear', 'Low') remain anywhere in the RoB columns. 7. Save the updated file back to papers/extraction_table.csv preserving all 8 rows.
